labels.contractDays: Longer notice in the contract (days, optional)
labels.contractDaysHint: The law's period applies unless the contract sets a longer one.
labels.wageHint: Used to estimate pay in lieu of notice.
labels.compensation: Pay in lieu if no notice is given

notes.rules: Under Oman's Labour Law (Royal Decree 53/2023, Art. 38) on an indefinite contract either side gives written notice of 30 days for monthly-paid workers and 15 days for others, unless the contract says longer. Ending without notice means paying compensation for the notice period. Employer notice must be at least a month (Art. 36), and the worker gets 10 paid hours a week to look for work during notice (Art. 39).
notes.disclaimer: Estimate only. Pay in lieu is the monthly gross wage divided by 30, times the notice days. Fixed-term contracts and probation (up to 3 months for monthly-paid workers, 7 days' notice) follow different rules. Confirm with the Ministry of Labour.
